subject: English
passage: Traditional varnish removal on aged oil paintings relies on volatile organic solvents, but conservation scientists pursuing an environmentally sustainable alternative have developed enzyme-loaded hydrogels that selectively cleave aged varnish layers without abrading the underlying paint. The standard rinsing step required to neutralize residual enzymes after gel application generates considerable solvent waste and other unwanted byproducts, so adopting such a regimen would compromise the ecological promise of the hydrogel approach. To address this, Olivia Sullivan, Louis Colombo, and colleagues engineered the hydrogel to incorporate self-quenching enzyme variants, thereby allowing the gel to neutralize itself in situ without any external rinse.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: To describe a consideration that led the researchers to employ an alternative approach to neutralizing a hydrogel that allowed them to achieve their main goal as presented in the text.
choices.B: To indicate the characteristic of conventional solvent-based removal methods that makes those methods poorly suited to achieve the researchers' main goal as presented in the text.
choices.C: To illustrate how the researchers adapted the hydrogel approach to overcome a potential impediment to their main goal as presented in the text.
choices.D: To concede that the researchers' main goal as described in the text will be challenging to achieve due to the standard neutralizing approach being impractical for use on a hydrogel.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The text establishes that conservation scientists are pursuing an environmentally sustainable alternative to solvent-based varnish removal by developing enzyme-loaded hydrogels. The underlined portion indicates that using the standard rinsing step to neutralize residual enzymes would generate considerable solvent waste, thereby compromising the ecological aim of the hydrogel approach. This consideration is precisely what led Sullivan, Colombo, and colleagues to employ an alternative approach — engineering self-quenching enzyme variants that neutralize in situ — which allowed them to achieve their main goal of an ecologically sustainable removal method.
